description: Inspired by the Goddess of the Moon, magic and crossroads, Hecate. We are here because it is our destiny to meet each other and complete this project together.
summary: Lunar Survival is an interactive educational game mainly designed for young children aged 7 to 12. Players take on the role of a lunar base crew tasked with surviving for three days against harsh space conditions, such as solar flares and incoming plasma clouds and limited resources. By making one critical system choice per day, selecting between activation of In-Situ Resource Utilization (ISRU), Environmental Control and Life Support Systems (ECLSS), or Radiation Shielding (RS) helps kids learn how difficult it is to survive at Lunar outpost while in an emergency situation. This project aim to make complex space concepts accessible and fun for kids visually, sparking early curiosity in STEM and creative solutions through simple, visual decision making.

How It Works & Creativity

Lunar Survival challenges players to survive three days on the Moon. Each day, players check the Readings panel (tracking power, life support, and resources), a real data Radiation Level graph, and incoming Status Reports. Based on the daily threat, like a solar storm, the player can press only one of three buttons per day: ISRU (to gather resources), ECLSS (to maintain air and life support), or RS (to block radiation). We paired retro pixel-art visuals with clear icons (a leaf, recycling symbol, and shield) and simple on-screen tutorials so young kids can easily grasp cause and effect.

Figure above shows one of the frame in Lunar Survival

Tools & Design Factor

We designed and prototyped the entire game interface, interactive states, and pixel graphics using Figma, incorporating actual NASA radiation data to ground the gameplay in real science. Because our target audience is aged 7 to 12, our team focused heavily on visual clarity, minimal text, color-coded feedback, and limiting choices to one button per day so young players aren't overwhelmed.

Benefits & Impact

The game introduces toddlers and young kids to real-world NASA space-habitat systems in a playful, low-pressure way. It builds early critical thinking, pattern recognition, and STEM awareness by turning complex astronaut survival mechanics into an intuitive kids' game.
